# Part 2: Filled Example, P-1102

## 1. Identification
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Module tag | P-1102 |
| Description / service | Transfer pump, mix tank T-110 → hold tank T-120 |
| Module type | VFD Pump (template rev 1) |
| P&ID reference | `<dwg no.>` |
| Narrative revision / date / author | Rev A / `<date>` / `<author>` |

## 2. Purpose
P-1102 transfers product from mix tank T-110 to hold tank T-120 at a speed set by the batch system. It is protected against running dry on T-110 and against overfilling T-120.

## 3. Associated Tags
| Role | Tag | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Run command | P-1102 run command | `<tag per I/O list>` |
| Speed reference | P-1102 speed ref | Source: batch system (Auto), operator (Manual) |
| Speed feedback | `<tag>` | |
| Run feedback | `<tag>` | |
| VFD fault | `<tag>` | |
| Local/remote status | `<tag>` | |
| Suction protection | LSL-110 | T-110 low level switch. *Confirm contact state when level is low (assumed: contact opens on low or wire break).* |
| Discharge pressure | PT-1102 | Analog |
| Destination protection | LSH-120 | T-120 high level switch. *Confirm contact state when level is high (assumed: contact opens on high or wire break).* |

## 4. Modes and Command Sources
| Mode | Start/stop | Speed | Interlocks active? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Auto | Batch system | Batch speed reference | Yes |
| Manual | Operator (HMI) | Operator | Yes |
| Out of Service | None | None | Pump held stopped |

- Switching from Auto to Manual while running: the pump keeps running at the current speed, and the operator takes over.
- Switching to Out of Service while running: the pump performs a normal stop.

## 5. Start Permissives
| # | Permissive | Source | Alarm DB ref |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | T-110 level above low (LSL-110 healthy) | LSL-110 | `<ID>` |
| 2 | T-120 level not high (LSH-120 healthy) | LSH-120 | `<ID>` |
| 3 | VFD ready, no fault | VFD fault | `<ID>` |
| 4 | Local/remote selector in remote | Local/remote status | — |
| 5 | Not Out of Service; no latched trip pending reset | Internal | — |
| 6 | Minimum off-time elapsed | Internal | per parameter sheet |

## 6. Run Interlocks (Trips)
| # | Condition | Source | Delay | Action | Reset | Alarm DB ref |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | T-110 low level (dry-run) | LSL-110 | per alarm DB | Immediate stop | Manual; level must be restored first | `<ID>` |
| 2 | T-120 high level | LSH-120 | per alarm DB | Normal stop | Auto-clears when level clears; the batch must re-request the start | `<ID>` |
| 3 | Discharge pressure high-high (dead-head or blocked line) | PT-1102 | per alarm DB | Immediate stop | Manual | `<ID>` |
| 4 | Discharge pressure low after the proving period (loss of prime or line break) | PT-1102 | per alarm DB, enabled after proving | Immediate stop | Manual | `<ID>` |
| 5 | VFD fault | VFD fault | none | Stop (drive-initiated) | Manual | `<ID>` |
| 6 | Run feedback lost while commanded | Run feedback | per alarm DB | Stop | Manual | `<ID>` |
| 7 | PT-1102 bad quality | PT-1102 | per alarm DB | Stop | Manual, after the signal recovers | `<ID>` |

*Open item: whether trips 3 and 4 are Stop or alarm-only (see section 14).*

## 7. Start Sequence
1. Confirm Auto or Manual mode and all permissives in section 5.
2. Set the speed reference to the requested value, limited to the min/max in the parameter sheet. The VFD acceleration ramp applies.
3. Issue the run command.
4. Run feedback must be received within the confirmation window. If not, raise the run-fail alarm and stop.
5. Start a pressure proving timer. During proving, the low-pressure trip (6.4) is shielded. If PT-1102 has not exceeded the proving threshold when the timer expires, trip on trip 4.
6. After proving, release the pump to speed control, with all interlocks live.

## 8. Speed Control
- **Auto:** the speed reference comes from the batch system, clamped to min/max limits and rate-limited per the parameter sheet.
- **Manual:** the operator enters the speed setpoint on the HMI, with the same clamps.
- **Reference lost or bad quality (Auto):** hold the last good speed, raise an alarm, and notify the batch. The pump stops if the condition persists beyond the alarm DB delay. *Confirm with process.*
- **Speed deviation:** raise an alarm when the feedback deviates from the reference beyond the alarm DB limit (`<ID>`) after the ramp settles.

## 9. Stop Sequence
- **Normal stop** (batch request, operator stop, T-120 high level, Out of Service): ramp down per the VFD deceleration setting, then drop the run command.
- **Trip stop** (LSL-110, PT-1102 trips, VFD fault, run feedback loss): remove the run command immediately. The VFD coasts or follows its own trip mode.
- No post-stop actions are required beyond status reporting to the batch.

## 10. Alarms
| Alarm DB ID | Name | Cause | Auto-clears? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<ID>` | T-110 Low Level – P-1102 Tripped | LSL-110 indicates low while running or commanded | No |
| `<ID>` | T-120 High Level – P-1102 Stopped | LSH-120 indicates high | Yes |
| `<ID>` | P-1102 Discharge Pressure High-High | PT-1102 above the high-high setpoint | No |
| `<ID>` | P-1102 Discharge Pressure Low / No Prime | PT-1102 below the setpoint after proving | No |
| `<ID>` | P-1102 Fail to Run | No run feedback after the start command | No |
| `<ID>` | P-1102 VFD Fault | VFD fault input active | No |
| `<ID>` | P-1102 Speed Deviation | Feedback vs. reference out of tolerance | Yes |
| `<ID>` | PT-1102 Bad Quality | Signal out of range or failed | Yes |

## 11. Fault Handling and Restart
- **Power loss or controller restart:** the pump stays stopped. The batch must re-request the start.
- **After a trip:** the operator must acknowledge and reset. Manual-reset trips cannot clear while the cause is still active.
- **Start limits:** max starts per hour and min off-time per the parameter sheet.
- **LSL-110 and LSH-120 wire break:** treated as the unsafe state (low / high), which blocks the start and trips the pump.

## 12. Bypass / Override Policy
No bypass of LSL-110, LSH-120, or the PT-1102 trips from the HMI. *If maintenance needs a bypass, it must go through a controlled change process (see section 14).*

## 13. Interface to Batch
- **Requests accepted:** Start, Stop, Speed setpoint.
- **Status returned:** Ready, Running, Faulted/Tripped, and a trip reason code (low T-110, high T-120, pressure, VFD, other).
- **High T-120:** the pump stops and reports "Stopped – destination full". The batch decides the next step; the pump does not restart automatically.
- **Request timeout:** if the pump doesn't report Running within the confirmation window, the batch is notified of the failure.

## 14. Open Items / Assumptions
1. Confirm the contact states (fail-safe behavior) for LSL-110 and LSH-120.
2. Confirm that trips 3 and 4 should stop the pump, versus alarm only. Low pressure is sometimes alarm-only if the process tolerates it.
3. Confirm the behavior on loss or bad quality of the batch speed reference (hold last vs. fixed speed vs. stop).
4. Confirm the pressure proving threshold and time with commissioning data.
5. All setpoints, delays, priorities, and tag addresses are to be taken from the I/O list and alarm DB. None are duplicated here.

---

**Suggestions for rollout:**
- Keep section numbering identical across all VFD pump narratives so reviewers and FAT testers can diff them.
- Section 6 and section 10 can double as FAT test-case lists, with one test per row.
- The "Alarm DB ref" columns are the link to your spreadsheets. If you can export those IDs, a script could fill or check them automatically.

I can make equivalent templates for the on/off valve, modulating valve, and agitator types if you want them to share the same section structure.
